name: @rebodocs/mcp

tools.name: open_document
tools.description: Opens a Word file (.docx) to read it and change it. It is kept in memory: nothing is written until save_document. Gives its overview.

tools.name: new_document
tools.description: Starts an empty document, to write in and save. Gives it the path it will be saved to.

path.description: Where it will be saved: a path ending in .docx.

tools.name: save_document
tools.description: Writes a document to a file: Word (.docx), PDF (.pdf) or Markdown (.md), by the ending of the path. A DOCX that was opened keeps everything that was not changed exactly as it was. With "editor" as the document, it saves what is open in the editor. It does not write over a file that is there unless "overwrite" is true: saving a copy under a new name is the safe way.

document.description: Which document: the path of a file opened with open_document, or "editor" for the one open in the editor in the browser ("editor:2" for the second, when several editors are connected: list_documents names them). Left out, it is the last file opened, or the editor when no file is open.

path.description: Where to write. Left out, the file the document was opened from.

overwrite.description: Write over a file that is already there. False when left out.

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Undoes the last changes the tools made to a file that is open, one at a time or several: the way back from a mistake without opening the file again and losing the rest. Up to 50 changes. In the editor in the browser, each change is a step the person undoes there.

document.description: The path of the file. Left out, the last file opened.

steps.description: How many changes to undo. 1 when left out.

tools.name: list_documents
tools.description: The documents that can be worked on now: the files that are open, with whether each has changes not saved, and whether an editor is connected.

tools.name: close_document
tools.description: Forgets a file that is open, with any changes that were not saved.

tools.name: get_overview
tools.description: A summary of the document: how long it is, its headings with the paragraph each is at, its template variables, its notes and its paragraph styles. Start here.

document.description: Which document: the path of a file opened with open_document, or "editor" for the one open in the editor in the browser ("editor:2" for the second, when several editors are connected: list_documents names them). Left out, it is the last file opened, or the editor when no file is open.

tools.name: read_document
tools.description: The text of the document, one paragraph a line, each with its number in brackets and, in parentheses, its style and its table cell when it has them. A long document comes in parts: ask for the next with "from".

from.description: The first paragraph to read. 1 when left out.

to.description: The last paragraph to read. The end when left out.

area.description: Which part of the document: its text ("body", when left out), the header or the footer every page shows, the ones the first page has to itself when the document gives it its own ("first_header", "first_footer": get_overview says whether it does), a note at the foot of the page ("footnote", with area_footnote), or a text box ("textbox", with area_textbox). Each has paragraphs numbered from 1 of its own.

area_section.description: With "area", in a document of several sections: the section, from 1, whose own header or footer it is (get_overview says which have their own). Left out, the document's: those of the last section, which every section without its own shows.

area_footnote.description: With area "footnote": the number of the note, as read_document shows it in [^n].

area_endnote.description: With area "endnote": which note at the end, from 1 for the first (the one shown [^i]), as read_document lists them.

area_textbox.description: With area "textbox": the number of the text box, as get_overview lists them.

document.description: Which document: the path of a file opened with open_document, or "editor" for the one open in the editor in the browser ("editor:2" for the second, when several editors are connected: list_documents names them). Left out, it is the last file opened, or the editor when no file is open.

tools.name: read_formatting
tools.description: How paragraphs look: for each, its style, alignment, indents, the room before and after it and its line spacing; then each stretch of its text that looks different, with its font, its size and whether it is bold, italic, underlined or coloured. Read it before rewriting or adding text that has to look like what is there.

from.description: The first paragraph. 1 when left out.

to.description: The last paragraph. 20 after "from" when left out.

tools.name: compare_documents
tools.description: What changed between this document and another version of it in a .docx file ("path"): the paragraphs put in, taken out and changed, of the text and of its headers, footers, notes at the foot of the page and text boxes, and the notes on the text (as add_note makes), with what was taken out as [-…-] and what was put in as {+…+}. Tracked changes are compared as if accepted, as Word does. By default the file is the earlier version; with "file_is" "later", it is the later one.

path.description: The path of the other version, a .docx file.

file_is.description: Whether the file is the earlier version (the default) or the later one.

document.description: Which document: the path of a file opened with open_document, or "editor" for the one open in the editor in the browser ("editor:2" for the second, when several editors are connected: list_documents names them). tools.name: read_pages
tools.description: How the document falls on its pages, as it prints: for each page, the paragraphs on it, how it starts and ends and how much room is left at its foot; and what may want mending: a paragraph cut by the end of a page, a heading left at the foot of one with its text on the next, a page with only a line or two, a table that runs over pages, a page with nothing on it. Read it after changes that move text, before a document goes out.

from.description: The first page, from 1. 1 when left out.

to.description: The last page. 30 after "from" when left out.

tools.name: replace_text
tools.description: Puts a text in place of another, in the formatting of what was there: its font, its size and its marks. The text to find has to be inside one paragraph. An empty "replace" deletes it. To write a whole paragraph anew, as in a translation, rewrite_paragraph keeps more of its look.

find.description: The exact text to act on, as it reads in the document. Capital and small letters count.

paragraph.description: Only look in this paragraph (its number from read_document).

occurrence.description: Which match to use when the text is found more than once: 1 for the first.

replace.description: The text to put in its place.

all.description: Replace every match, not just one.

tools.name: rewrite_paragraph
tools.description: Writes the whole text of a paragraph anew, as to translate it or say it otherwise, and keeps how it looks: its style, alignment, indents and spacing, and the font, size and colour most of its text has. Words that were set apart (bold, italic…) are kept so by giving the text in "segments". A paragraph with a picture is changed with replace_text instead.

text.description: Its new text, all in the look most of it had.

segments.description: Instead of "text": the text in pieces, each with what sets it apart from the rest (bold, italic, a colour…), to keep the words that were bold bold. The pieces are joined as they are: put the spaces in them.

color.description: The colour of the text, as six hex digits: C0392B.

highlight.description: The colour behind the text: one of FFFF00, 00FF00, 00FFFF, FF00FF, 0000FF, FF0000, 000080, 008080, 008000, 800080, 800000, 808000, 808080, C0C0C0, 000000; "none" to take it away.

With "like_paragraph" a new one looks like a paragraph that is there: its alignment, indents, spacing, list, and the font, size and colour of most of its text. Text between double braces, like {{cliente}}, is a template variable.

after_paragraph.description: The number of the paragraph to insert after; 0 to insert at the start.

like_paragraph.description: A paragraph every new one looks like, unless it says another.

tools.name: edit_document
tools.description: Makes several changes in one go, each as the tool it names would make it, and all of them or none. Every paragraph number in them is the one read_document showed before the first edit: the numbers do not move as the edits before insert or delete paragraphs, so there is no need to read again between them. A text to find is looked for as the document is when its edit comes. Each edit is an object with "tool" (replace_text, rewrite_paragraph, insert_paragraphs, delete_paragraphs, set_style, set_list, format_text, format_paragraphs, set_link, add_note, insert_page_break, move_section, set_cell_text, renumber_clauses) and the arguments of that tool beside it. The text of the document only: for a header or a footer, use each tool alone with "area".

edits.description: The changes, in the order to make them.

tool.description: The tool that makes this change. Its arguments go beside "tool".

document.description: Which document: the path of a file opened with open_document, or "editor" for the one open in the editor in the browser ("editor:2" for the second, when several editors are connected: list_documents names them). Left out, it is the last file opened, or the editor when no file is open.

tools.name: move_section
tools.description: Moves a heading and everything under it, down to the next heading of its level or above (a clause with its text, a chapter with its clauses), to another place, as dragging it in the outline of the editor does. The paragraphs keep their look, their notes and their pictures. After it, renumber_clauses puts the numbers of the headings in order.

paragraph.description: The heading of what to move, as read_document numbers it. get_overview lists the headings.

before.description: The paragraph it goes before, as numbered now. Left out, it goes to the end of the document.

document.description: Which document: the path of a file opened with open_document, or "editor" for the one open in the editor in the browser ("editor:2" for the second, when several editors are connected: list_documents names them). Left out, it is the last file opened, or the editor when no file is open.

tools.name: renumber_clauses
tools.description: Puts in order the numbers written at the start of the headings of clauses, after one was put in, taken out or moved: "Primera.", "Segunda."… in words, "CLÁUSULA 3.", or "IV.", each kept as it is written (its capitals, "Primera" or "Primero", "Décima Primera" or "Undécima"). The headings of one series are those that begin the same way and have the same style; the longest is renumbered, or the one of "paragraph". It says the places of the text that name a clause by its number ("según la cláusula Tercera"), for you to check: it does not change them.

paragraph.description: A heading of the series to renumber, when the document has more than one. The longest when left out.

start.description: The number of the first. 1 when left out.

document.description: Which document: the path of a file opened with open_document, or "editor" for the one open in the editor in the browser ("editor:2" for the second, when several editors are connected: list_documents names them). Left out, it is the last file opened, or the editor when no file is open.

tools.name: set_cell_text

A new line in "text" starts another paragraph in the cell. The way to fill the cells of a row just put in.

cell.description: The cell in that row, from 1.

text.description: What the cell says. Empty to leave it empty.

tools.name: format_paragraphs
tools.description: Changes how paragraphs sit on the page: their alignment, indents, the room before and after them, their line spacing, their tab stops, and whether they keep with the next one. Give only what is to change.

to.description: The last one. The same as "from" when left out.

indent_left_cm.description: From the left margin, in centimetres.

indent_right_cm.description: From the right margin, in centimetres.

first_line_cm.description: How much further in the first line starts, in centimetres; below 0 for a hanging indent.

space_before_pt.description: Room above the paragraph, in points.

space_after_pt.description: Room below the paragraph, in points.

keep_with_next.description: Keep it on the same page as the next paragraph, as a heading.

keep_lines_together.description: Keep all its lines on one page: the paragraph goes whole to the next page rather than being cut.

tab_stops.description: All the tab stops the paragraphs are to have, in place of the ones they have; [] for none. A tab in the text goes to the next one; past them, every 1.27 cm.

at_cm.description: From the left margin, in centimetres.

align.description: Whether the text after the tab starts there, is centred on it, ends there or has its decimal point there.

leader.description: What fills the room of the tab, as the dots of an index.

instructions: Tools to read and edit Word documents (.docx). Work on a file with open_document, or on the document a person has open in the editor in their browser by giving "editor" as the document. Paragraphs go by number: read_document shows them, and the numbers move when paragraphs are inserted or deleted, so read again before using a number after such a change; edit_document makes several changes at once in the numbers of one reading. To change a text, give it exactly as it reads. The header and the footer are read and changed with "area". Changes to a file stay in memory until save_document; prefer saving a copy to writing over the original. To review a document without changing it, use add_note.
